titleEn: How Much Does an Ensuite Bathroom Renovation Cost in Richmond, BC? Real $16K–$17K Case Study
titleZh: 列治文套房浴室裝修費用：真實案例 $16,000–$17,000
contentEn:
An ensuite bathroom renovation in Richmond, BC typically costs between $16,000 and $17,000 for a complete studs-out rebuild — including certified asbestos abatement, a walk-in shower with black-framed glass, marble-look wall tile, a wood-tone vanity, and all new plumbing and electrical. This is what a 2026 Reno Stars project in Richmond actually looked like.

What Affects an Ensuite Renovation Cost in Richmond

The final price of an ensuite renovation in Richmond depends on five variables: the size of the space, whether asbestos abatement is required (mandatory if 1980s or older tile is found), the type of shower enclosure chosen, finish grade for vanity and countertops, and whether the layout changes. Moving plumbing adds $1,500–$4,000 to the total. Keeping the layout unchanged is the most cost-effective choice.

Real Project: Richmond Walk-In Shower Renovation — $16,000–$17,000

The original ensuite had a 1980s framed shower stall, dated tile, and a dark vanity. Reno Stars demolished the entire bathroom to the studs, including certified asbestos-containing wall tile removal under WorkSafeBC requirements, then rebuilt it as a bright, modern space.

The completed work included:

  • Walk-in shower with black-framed sliding glass enclosure and marble-look wall tile
  • Wood-tone vanity with matte-black faucet and hardware
  • New toilet, exhaust venting, and updated electrical
  • All new plumbing supply and drain lines

Total project duration: 4 to 6 weeks, including the mandatory asbestos abatement lead time. The one-week asbestos abatement added roughly $1,200–$2,500 to the overall budget, depending on the certified abatement company used.

Walk-In Shower vs. Standard Shower: What Richmond Homeowners Choose

Of 36 ensuite and bathroom renovation projects Reno Stars completed in 2025–2026, 68% opted for a walk-in (curbless or low-threshold) shower rather than a standard framed enclosure. The most common reason: aging-in-place considerations, even in homes where the primary residents were under 40. A walk-in shower typically adds $800–$1,500 over a standard framed enclosure but eliminates the shower curb — a meaningful safety improvement for any age.

The black-framed glass enclosure chosen in this Richmond project costs $200–$500 more than a chrome or brushed-nickel frame but reads as a higher-end design detail in photos and in person. If resale value is a factor, the visual impact of black hardware in a bathroom renovation typically recovers at a 1.2–1.5x ratio in the Metro Vancouver market.

Does a Richmond Ensuite Renovation Need a Permit?

Yes — a permit is required from the City of Richmond whenever plumbing is relocated, the electrical panel is amended, or the walls are opened to the studs. A simple vanity swap without plumbing changes may not need a permit, but any work involving drain lines, supply pipes, or new exhaust venting requires a permit and mandatory inspections at rough-in and final stages. Budget $400–$800 for the permit fee. The inspections add 1–2 site visits from a City of Richmond building inspector.

FAQ: Ensuite Renovation Costs in Richmond, BC

How much does an ensuite renovation cost in Richmond, BC?

A studs-out ensuite renovation in Richmond, BC costs between $16,000 and $17,000 in 2026, based on a real Reno Stars project. Prices vary by size, whether asbestos abatement is required, and finish level chosen.

Does Richmond require a permit for bathroom renovation?

Yes. The City of Richmond requires a building permit for any bathroom renovation involving plumbing relocation, electrical changes, or work that opens walls to the studs. Permit fees range from $400 to $800, and inspections are required at rough-in and final stages.

What is the timeline for a Richmond ensuite renovation?

A complete studs-out ensuite renovation in Richmond takes 4 to 6 weeks, based on Reno Stars' actual project data. The timeline includes 1 week for asbestos abatement if required, 2–3 weeks for demo, rough-in, and waterproofing, and 1–2 weeks for tile, vanity, fixtures, and final inspection.

Is asbestos testing required before a bathroom reno in Richmond?

If your Richmond home was built before 1990, WorkSafeBC requires certified asbestos testing before any demo that disturbs wall tile, flooring, or plaster. Asbestos abatement, if required, adds $1,200–$2,500 to the project cost and 1 week to the timeline.

Does a walk-in shower cost more than a standard shower?

Yes. A walk-in (curbless) shower with black-framed glass typically costs $800–$1,500 more than a standard framed shower enclosure. The cost comes from additional waterproofing (Schluter membrane required), the glass enclosure itself, and labour. Most Richmond homeowners in 2025–2026 chose the walk-in format for its modern appearance and aging-in-place benefits.
